info.title: CLARA API
info.summary: Clinical Logbook for Automated Research Assistance — REDCap API replacement
info.description:
Two surfaces (REQ-API-001): the REDCap-compatible data API at `POST /api/` (and `GET /api/`) with the caller token as the `token` parameter in the request body or query string (never an `Authorization` header, REQ-API-010), and the administration API under `/api/v1/`. The administration surface is reachable only from the trusted internal path (REQ-TECH-018): every request carries a valid `X-Internal-Service-Token` and — except for the pre-authentication endpoints of §4.3 — the authoritative `X-Internal-User-Id` of the acting user. The browser MUST NOT call `/api/v1/*` directly (GD-1).

Conventions (`Design/API_Endpoints_Design.md` §1): UTC and UTF-8; system timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC; absent optionals are `null`. Administration errors share the shape `{ "error": <stable code>, "message": <human-readable>, "status": <http status> }`; data-API errors are rendered in the requested response format (`json`: `{ "error": "…" }`, `csv`: a single line).

This document is hand-maintained (REQ-TECH-004, REQ-API-002) and served at `GET /openapi.json`; the interactive UI is the vendored Swagger UI bundle at `GET /docs`.

servers.description: The Go API process. nginx routes only POST /api/ (plus the PHP application) publicly; /api/v1/* and the documentation endpoints stay off the public network (Technology_Stack_Design.md §5).

post.description:
One endpoint dispatched by the `content` parameter with an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body. With `content=record`, a call carrying `data` is an import, one without it an export; deletion needs `action=delete`. Unknown parameters are accepted and ignored, never rejected (REQ-API-017). The token is the `token` parameter — never read from an `Authorization` header (REQ-API-010). Survey-link tokens are accepted only for the calls that render and fill their (record, instrument, event) triple: `content=metadata` (that instrument only) and a record import scoped to that record, instrument and event; everything else is 403 `Permission denied` (§3.10, REQ-API-083). A row submitted with a link token names none of that triple — the API takes record, instrument and event from the link, which is how the public survey page submits without learning the record identifier — while a row naming a different one is 403 rather than retargeted.

Error bodies are rendered in the requested response format (§3.2): 401 `Invalid token`, 400 `Invalid content`, 403 `Permission denied`, 403 `Project in analysis mode` for writes to an analysis-mode project, 429 `Rate limit exceeded` (with `Retry-After`). A request over the body-size or parameter bound is 400 naming the limit it crossed, answered before the token is looked at — never a 401 (REQ-API-144).

The Request body examples carry one call per common shape — export (all records, `records[]`, `fields[]`, `forms[]`, `events[]`, combined filters, `filterLogic`, labels, repeating instances, `type=wide`, CSV), import and delete, plus the metadata contents. The 200 response examples with the same title show the answers; all of them come from one example project (events `baseline_arm_1` and `6_month_arm_1`; instruments `intake`, `imaging`, and `exclusions` repeating at baseline).

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: text/csv is the REDCap default rendering; application/json selects JSON.

requestBody.description: One `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body — the examples are shown unencoded; URL-encode each value when sending. `token` and `content` are required; every other parameter is optional.

recordExportAll.description: No filter: every record visible to the token holder (data access group rule, REQ-API-092), one row per (record, event) and one per repeating instance.

recordExportRecords.description: Indexed array syntax `records[0]=…`; repeated `records=…` works as well (REQ-API-015).

recordExportFields.description: A checkbox named in `fields[]` exports all of its `<field>___<code>` columns (REQ-EXP-053). A `fields[]` export carries no `<instrument>_complete` columns (REQ-API-134). The record identifier is always included (REQ-API-028).

recordExportForms.description: Each instrument's block ends with `<instrument>_complete` (REQ-API-134); at an event the instrument is not mapped to that cell is empty. The record identifier is always included, even when its instrument is not among `forms[]` (REQ-API-028).

recordExportEvents.description: Unique event names as returned by `content=event`.

recordExportFilterLogic.description: Branching-logic expression (§3.6.3); a malformed expression is 400 before any output (REQ-API-025).

recordExportLabels.summary: Labels instead of codes: rawOrLabel=label, rawOrLabelHeaders=label
recordExportLabels.description: Choice codes become their labels; checkbox columns read `Checked`/`Unchecked` as in REDCap (REQ-EXP-053); `redcap_event_name` carries the event's name — with `(Arm <n>: <arm name>)` in a project with several arms (REQ-API-028); headers become `<Field Label>` and `<Field Label>, <Choice Label>` (REQ-API-027).

recordExportCheckboxLabel.description: With `rawOrLabel=label` and `exportCheckboxLabel=true` a checked box exports its choice label and an unchecked one an empty string (REQ-EXP-053, REQ-API-016).

recordList.summary: Records — list of records and events: fields[]=record_id
recordList.description: The record identifier alone: one row per (record, event) holding data (REQ-API-028).

recordExportRepeating.description: Each instance is its own row naming `redcap_repeat_instrument` and `redcap_repeat_instance` (a JSON number); the event's own row leaves the repeating instrument's columns empty. The two repeat columns exist only in projects with a repeating instrument (REQ-API-155).

recordExportWide.description: One row per record, opening with the record identifier; a field mapped to several events repeats as `<field>_<unique_event_name>` (§3.6.2).

recordExportCsv.description: `format=csv` (or no format at all) answers `text/csv` — see the `text/csv` media type of the 200 response.

importJsonCount.description: Rows are flat (no `form_name`): every key is stored on its own instrument. A project with events needs `redcap_event_name` (or `event_name`) per row (REQ-API-138). Numbers may be sent as JSON numbers. `overwriteBehavior` and `forceAutoNumber` are accepted and ignored (REQ-API-017).

importIndexed.summary: Import — indexed rows data[i][key], per-row result
importIndexed.description: Without `returnContent=count` the answer is one result row per data row (REQ-API-034): `import_record_id` 1 added, 2 updated, 0 rejected with the reason in `import_form_name`. A rejected row stores nothing; the other rows are applied (REQ-API-035).

importRepeating.summary: Import — instances of a repeating instrument
importRepeating.description: `redcap_repeat_instrument` + `redcap_repeat_instance` fill that instance; instance 1 is the first instance's storage (REQ-API-155).

deleteFieldsAtEvent.summary: Delete — fields of one record at one event
deleteFieldsAtEvent.description: `action=delete` with `records[]`, narrowed by `events[]` and `fields[]` (REQ-API-036). `records[]` is required — an unscoped delete is 400.

deleteInstance.summary: Delete — one instance of a repeating instrument
deleteInstance.description: `repeat_instance` narrows the delete to that instance (REQ-API-155).

event.description: All events of all arms in the canonical per-arm order (GD-15, REQ-API-020).

formEventMapping.description: Which instrument is collected at which event (REQ-API-021).

metadataForms.summary: Fields — data dictionary of selected forms: content=metadata&forms[]
metadataForms.description: One row per field; a checkbox stays one row with its choices (REQ-API-019, REQ-EXP-053).

exportFieldNamesForms.summary: Fields — field names of selected forms: content=exportFieldNames&forms[]

200.description: The result of the requested `content`. The JSON shape depends on `content` — see the examples. Record imports answer per-row result rows (or `{"count": N}` with `returnContent=count`, REQ-API-142); validation failures are per-record, not request-level (REQ-API-034).

schema.description: Result rows; `generateNextRecordName` answers a single object and `returnContent=count` answers `{"count": N}`.

importResultRows.summary: content=record import — result rows (REQ-API-034; import_record_id 1 added, 2 updated, 0 validation error)

value.import_form_name: Validation error: age: TYPE_INVALID — value "abc" is not a valid integer; status: CHOICE_INVALID — value "9" is not a choice of "status"

schema.description: The same result as CSV — the REDCap default when neither `format` nor `returnFormat` says otherwise. Streamed, quoted per standard CSV rules, honoring `csvDelimiter` (REQ-API-029).

get.summary: REDCap-compatible data API via query string (REQ-API-009)
get.description:
`GET /api/` with the same parameters in the query string MUST also work. Behaviour, responses and errors are identical to `POST /api/`.

Example calls — the answers are the 200 response examples shared with `POST /api/`; `[` and `]` may be sent unencoded or as `%5B`/`%5D`:

- **All records, flat** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat`
- **Selected records** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&records[0]=8DISC041&records[1]=8DISC042`
- **Selected fields** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&fields[0]=record_id&fields[1]=age&fields[2]=features`
- **Whole forms** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&forms[0]=intake&forms[1]=imaging`
- **Selected events** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&events[0]=6_month_arm_1`
- **Combined filters** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&records[0]=8DISC041&fields[0]=record_id&fields[1]=series_count&events[0]=6_month_arm_1`
- **filterLogic** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&forms[0]=intake&filterLogic=%5Bage%5D%20%3E%2040`
- **Record list** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&fields[0]=record_id`
- **Labels** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&fields[0]=record_id&fields[1]=status&rawOrLabel=label&rawOrLabelHeaders=label`
- **Checkbox choice labels** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=json&type=flat&fields[0]=features&rawOrLabel=label&exportCheckboxLabel=true`
- **CSV** — `/api/?token=…&content=record&format=csv&type=flat&fields[0]=record_id&fields[1]=age&csvDelimiter=%3B`
- **Events** — `/api/?token=…&content=event&format=json`
- **Forms × events** — `/api/?token=…&content=formEventMapping&format=json`
- **Repeating forms** — `/api/?token=…&content=repeatingFormsEvents&format=json`
- **Fields of a form** — `/api/?token=…&content=metadata&format=json&forms[0]=intake`
- **Field names of a form** — `/api/?token=…&content=exportFieldNames&format=json&forms[0]=intake`

A token in a URL can end up in proxy and server logs — prefer `POST /api/` with the token in the body.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Project API token or survey-link token (§3.10).

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Dispatches the call — with `content=record`, a call carrying `data` is an import, one without it an export; deletion needs `action=delete` (REQ-API-012).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only `delete` dispatches; `export`/`import` are accepted and never override the `data` rule (REQ-API-012).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `json` or `csv`; `csv` is REDCap's default rendering. A present `returnFormat` takes precedence (REQ-API-013).

parameters.name: returnFormat
parameters.description: Takes precedence over `format` for the response encoding (REQ-API-013).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: `flat` is normative — one row per (record, event); `wide` is the simplified compatibility mode (§3.6.2, DEV-API-1).

parameters.name: csvDelimiter
parameters.description: REDCap's set — tab as the character or by the name `tab`; empty value = comma. Any other value → 400 (REQ-API-029, REQ-EXP-013).

parameters.name: decimalCharacter
parameters.description: Record export: the decimal separator of calculated and floating-point values, in either format; empty value = the stored form (a period). Any other value → 400 (REQ-EXP-015).

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: Repeated values or the REDCap indexed syntax `records[0]=…` (REQ-API-015).

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Field names to export or delete; sent as `fields[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). A checkbox named here covers all of its `<field>___<code>` columns (REQ-EXP-053); a field-list export carries no `<instrument>_complete` column (REQ-API-134).

parameters.name: forms
parameters.description: Instrument unique names; sent as `forms[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). A record export returns each named instrument's whole field block, ending with its `<instrument>_complete` column (REQ-API-134); `content=metadata`/`exportFieldNames` restrict the dictionary to these instruments (REQ-API-083, REQ-API-022).

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Unique event names as returned by `content=event`; sent as `events[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). At an event an instrument is not mapped to the cell is empty (REQ-API-134).

parameters.name: filterLogic
parameters.description: Branching-logic expression filtering which records are returned; never changes the sensitivity level (REQ-API-025, §3.6.3).

parameters.name: rawOrLabel
parameters.description: Choice fields as codes or labels (REQ-API-027).

parameters.name: rawOrLabelHeaders
parameters.description: `both` renders each header as `<Field Label> (field_name)` (REQ-API-027).

parameters.name: exportCheckboxLabel
parameters.description: Record export with `rawOrLabel=label`: `true` writes a checked box's choice label (unchecked: empty); otherwise `Checked`/`Unchecked` (REQ-EXP-053).

post.description:
Called by the PHP application after successful OAuth2/LDAP authentication, or with `source: "local"` and the password for table-based login (GD-18). Exempt from `X-Internal-User-Id` (DEV-API-16); it still requires the service token. The API reports success and audit-logs it but MUST NOT create or store a session (GD-1).

Processing order: local credential check (or an unexpired `first_factor` handle standing in for the hash check where a second factor guards the account, REQ-API-131) → account-active rule (`account_expired` / `account_disabled`) → two-factor gate (`mfa_required`, `bad_mfa_code`, `tfa_enrollment_required`) → bootstrap-admin promotion → `auth_source`/`last_login_at` update → audit `login_success`. The returned user object carries the account's `session_epoch`, which the web layer keeps in the session it establishes (REQ-AUTH-074).

handle_mfa.summary: Second call of a two-factor challenge with the handle from verify-password (REQ-API-131)

race.summary: Finalizing call of a failed named-source credential race (DEV-API-5 detail)

401.description: `account_not_found` — no user row for the email (REQ-AUTH-006); `bad_password` — no stored hash or mismatch (the two are not distinguished, GD-18); `mfa_required` `{"error":"mfa_required","method":"totp|email"}`; `bad_mfa_code`; `tfa_enrollment_required` `{"error":"tfa_enrollment_required","user_id":<id>}` under `AUTH_REQUIRE_2FA`; `first_factor_expired` (REQ-API-131). All audit `login_failure` where applicable.

403.description: `account_disabled` (including auto-disable by the inactivity rule) or `account_expired` (`valid_until` passed) — REQ-AUTH-052/053.

post.summary: Side-effect-free password verify for the named-source credential race (§4.3, REQ-API-123, DEV-API-17)
post.description: Runs the login endpoint's hash check and account-active rule only — no `last_login_at`/`auth_source` write, no audit event, no user object; login finalizes exactly once through `/api/v1/auth/login`. Pre-authentication: service token only. For an account a second factor still guards, the `ok` answer carries the `first_factor` handle (5 minutes, bound to one user id) that the challenge's second login call presents in place of the password (REQ-API-131).

200.description: `status` ∈ `ok | bad_password | account_disabled | account_expired`. `first_factor` and `expires_in` appear only on `ok` for an account a second factor still guards.

post.description: Records the `logout` audit event. Destruction of the PHP session remains the PHP layer's responsibility, performed after this call (GD-1).

Called by the web layer when a session id it rotated away (REQ-AUTH-072) is presented again after the grace window — two parties held the same session (REQ-AUTH-073). The acting user is the account the old id belonged to, named by `X-Internal-User-Id` without `X-Internal-Session-Epoch`. The API raises the account's session epoch, which ends every session of the account at its next call (REQ-AUTH-074), and records `session_replay_detected` with the presenting address (never a session id). No body. The API keeps no session state (GD-1).

200.description: Every session of the account is ended.

post.summary: Request a password-reset link (Sequence H, REQ-API-119)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only (DEV-API-16). Always 202 with an identical body — whether or not a matching active local account exists (no enumeration, REQ-AUTH-062). When one does, emails the set-password link with a single-use `reset` token. Rate-limited per address and IP (default 3/15 min/address). Audit `password_reset_requested` (address + IP, never the token).

202.description: Accepted — identical body regardless of account existence.

post.summary: Set the new password with a reset token (REQ-API-120)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only. Constant-time hash verification, purpose `reset`, expiry, single use; success stores the argon2id hash, consumes the token, invalidates all outstanding tokens of the account, raises its session epoch (every session of the account ends, REQ-AUTH-074) and audits `password_reset_completed`. No temporary password exists (REQ-AUTH-062). Any failure — unknown, expired, consumed or wrong-purpose token — answers the generic 401 `invalid_setup_token` (causes are not distinguished).

post.summary: Accept an invitation — set the invited user's own password (REQ-API-121)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only. As `/api/v1/auth/password-reset/complete` for purpose `invite`; audits `invite_accepted`; generic 401 `invalid_setup_token` on any failure. Login afterwards runs the full second-factor gate (REQ-AUTH-060).

get.description: Requires `is_admin`; a call by a non-admin is rejected (403 `forbidden`).

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. A new account → 201; a disabled account with the same email is re-enabled → 200 (re-enabling resets the inactivity clock, REQ-AUTH-053). The optional password is stored only as an argon2id hash (REQ-AUTH-050), never returned or logged. Audit `user_created` (`re_enabled` flag, `valid_until`).

200.description: A disabled account with this email was re-enabled.

put.description: Requires `is_admin`; idempotent (REQ-API-042). Any change that would leave zero enabled administrators (an `is_admin` revocation, a disabling, or both in one call) is rejected 409 `conflict` with nothing written and no audit entry (REQ-API-136). `valid_days` re-sets `valid_until` (`0` → indefinite); `password` set/resets the local hash and an empty string clears it. Disabling a user denies the effective permissions of that user's API tokens at call time (REQ-AUTH-033). A password write or a disabling raises the account's session epoch, ending its sessions (REQ-AUTH-074); the user object returned carries the new `session_epoch`. Audit `user_updated` with the changed attributes.

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Sends the invitation email with a single-use `invite` token to the account's address; a re-invite replaces any outstanding invite token (the old link dies). The token value is never in the response. 409 `smtp_not_configured` without a relay (the admin then sets the password directly). Audit `user_invited`.

put.description: Self-service. The current password is verified against `password_hash` first (failure → 401 `bad_password`, audit-logged, counted toward the REQ-AUTH-035 lockout), then the new argon2id hash is stored. Accounts without a local credential → 409 `no_local_credential`. The change raises the account's session epoch, ending every other session (REQ-AUTH-074); the answer carries the new value so the session that made the change can adopt it and stay signed in. Audit `password_changed`.

401.description: `bad_password` — the current password did not verify.

409.description: `no_local_credential` — the account has no local password.

get.description: Self-service; also valid in the pending-first-factor context under a mandate. Never returns the secret or a code.

200.description: The current method and enrollment time.

post.description: Returns the shared secret and its `otpauth://` URI — shown once; pending until confirmed.
A valid current RFC 6238 code activates `totp` and returns the recovery codes exactly once; a wrong code → 400 `bad_code`. Audit `tfa_enrolled`.

200.description: `totp` is active; recovery codes are returned once.

post.description: Sends a confirmation code to the account address via the SMTP relay; rate-limited per account.
Activates `email`, returns the recovery codes once. Audit `tfa_enrolled`.

200.description: `email` is active; recovery codes are returned once.

post.description: Requires a valid current code or recovery code; sets the method to `off` and clears secret/codes. Audit `tfa_disabled`.

Requires `is_admin`. Deletes the account's `user_two_factor` row back to `off` (lost device/email). No endpoint ever returns a secret, pending code, or recovery code outside its single enrollment/activation response. Also raises the account's session epoch, ending its sessions (REQ-AUTH-074); the answer names the new value, which the acting session adopts when it reset its own account. Audit `tfa_reset`.

get.description: Project visibility only (`is_admin` or member, REQ-AUTH-026); projects outside the acting user's visibility do not appear (REQ-API-007).

200.description: Dashboard summaries of every visible project.

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Creation is single-arm (REQ-DB-011, DEV-API-4): the API creates arm 1 only, together with its first event `baseline` (`unique_event_name = baseline_arm_1`, timepoint `period = 0`) and one instrument `instrument`. The removed attributes (`end_provision`, the `option_*` flags, `agreed_to_end_user_contract`, `event_names`) are rejected as unknown attributes (400 `invalid_request`). A duplicate `project_name` → 409. Audit `project_created`.

201.description: The created project (`id` + the supplied fields + `creation_time`).

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only` + project visibility. Full metadata plus structure plus the acting user's effective permissions — the same result the boundary applies to every call, surfaced so the PHP layer can gate rendering with the control absent from the DOM. Nothing is ever absent from `permissions.arms[]`/`grants[]`; the caller never infers a level from a missing entry (REQ-AUTH-069). This read authorizes nothing; every endpoint re-checks at call time (REQ-AUTH-033).

put.description: `project_admin` (an `is_admin` user is covered by REQ-AUTH-023). Body: any subset of the creation metadata fields — omitted fields are unchanged (idempotent, REQ-API-042). A duplicate `project_name` → 409. Metadata changes are audit-logged with old and new values (`project_updated`).

200.description: The updated project object (same shape as GET, `permissions` included).

get.description: Requires `is_admin`. `role` is `null` for a role-less member (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022); `token_present` reports existence without revealing the value (REQ-API-005).

put.summary: Add, change role, rotate token or remove a member (REQ-API-054/055)
put.description: Requires `is_admin`. The single mutation point for membership, keyed on the body: `{"role": "data-entry"}` adds (201, with the new token returned once); `{"role": null}` makes the member role-less; `{"rotate_token": true}` rotates — the previous token is invalid immediately; `{"remove": true}` removes the member and invalidates the token. Audit `membership_changed` plus `token_issued`/`token_rotated`/`token_revoked`. The token value never appears in logs or audit details.

200.description: Role change (member object), rotation (member object with the new token) or removal (`{"ok": true}`).

201.description: The member was added — the member object with the new token, returned once for display (REQ-API-055).

post.summary: Record that a just-issued token was shown (REQ-API-160)
post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Records that the acting administrator unmasked member `{uid}`'s just-issued token on the Members page: one `token_viewed` audit entry `{"member_email": "…"}` per call, separate from the add's `membership_changed` + `token_issued` (REQ-AUD-033). The body is empty or `{}`; any attribute is 400. No token value travels in either direction — the UI holds it from the add/rotation response and shows it only after this call succeeded. An unknown project or user, or a non-member, is 404 with nothing written.

get.description: Self-service: `{uid}` MUST equal the acting user and the acting user MUST be a member; any other case is a uniform 403 `forbidden` (never disclosed as missing, REQ-API-007). The value MUST NOT be logged. No audit event for the fetch itself — it is credential plumbing.

Any authenticated user acting on themselves. One entry per project the acting user is a **member** of, in project-id order, with the role name (`null` = role-less, full permissions — REQ-AUTH-022). Membership, not visibility: an administrator sees every project (REQ-API-049) but is listed here only where they are a member. No token value — every membership has one (REQ-API-005). Not audited.

200.description: The acting user's memberships, possibly empty.

post.summary: Reveal my own project token, audited (REQ-API-162)
post.description: Self-service: returns the acting member's own token for project `{id}` and records the view as one `token_viewed` audit entry `{"member_email": "<own address>"}` per call (REQ-AUD-033). The entry is written before the value is answered. The body is empty or `{}`; any attribute is 400. A project the acting user is not a member of — unknown or not — is the uniform 403 `forbidden` (REQ-API-007), with nothing written. The value MUST NOT be logged.

200.description: The member's API token; the view is recorded.

get.description: `is_admin`. Read-only, not audited. What only the API can see about the installation (INSTALL.md): its own configuration, the host it runs on, and the database through the application's own account. Facts, not ratings — the Control Panel's Configuration Check (REQ-UI-061) decides which value is a problem. A secret is never returned: `weak_secrets` names the variables whose value is empty, a development default, the `CHANGE_ME` placeholder or shorter than 16 characters. On SQLite only `connection`, `version` and `schema_version` of `database` are filled; a MariaDB value the account cannot read is `null`.

500.description: The database could not be read.

get.description: `is_admin`. Read-only, not audited. Per-route latency histograms and payload bytes, data API timings per content value, database statement timings with row counts per verb, connection dial and pool statistics, process memory and GC — sufficient to evaluate infrastructure and database extensions against the REQ-TECH-010/011 targets (API_Endpoints_Design.md §4.25). Values are measured in memory only and reset on restart. Labels come from closed sets (server-side route templates, the content vocabulary, a fixed verb enum): no path value, token or query text ever appears. Percentiles are estimates interpolated inside the histogram buckets.

`is_admin`. Read-only, not audited. Every source IP currently inside its blockout with the moment the block expires, plus the effective enable flag and both thresholds (API_Endpoints_Design.md §4.26). Live limiter state at request time: nothing is persisted and blocks reset on restart like the limiter itself. Source addresses are personal data shown to administrators only.

InternalServiceToken.name: X-Internal-Service-Token
InternalServiceToken.description: The shared service secret (REQ-AUTH-011/012): compared in constant time, never logged, enforced regardless of any other configuration (REQ-CFG-023). Missing or invalid → 401 `service_token_invalid` + audit `admin_rejected`. Configured per System_Configuration_Design.md §3.3.

InternalUserId.name: X-Internal-User-Id
InternalUserId.description: The acting user's id — authoritative for authorization (REQ-AUTH-013): the API applies that user's effective levels; the PHP layer adds none. Unknown or disabled user → 403 + audit `admin_rejected`. Set by the trusted PHP layer only; the proxy strips it from every externally-originated request. A call made for an established PHP session also carries `X-Internal-Session-Epoch` — the account's session epoch as the session recorded it at login (REQ-AUTH-074, REQ-API-147); when it differs from the stored value (or is not a number) the call is refused 401 `session_revoked` + audit `admin_rejected`. A call without it is not checked: the two-factor enrollment wizard's pending identity has no session yet (§2.7).

UserIdPath.name: uid
UserIdPath.description: User id of the project member.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor encoding the last-seen (created_at, id); from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_request` — malformed JSON body or a missing/invalid attribute (§4.2).

UnauthorizedServiceToken.description: `service_token_invalid` — missing/invalid X-Internal-Service-Token; or `session_revoked` — the call carried an `X-Internal-Session-Epoch` that no longer matches the acting account's (REQ-API-147; the web layer ends the session). Both audited `admin_rejected`.

AdminForbidden.description: `forbidden` — insufficient permission, or a project/record outside the acting user's visibility (uniform, never disclosed as missing — REQ-API-007); unknown/disabled acting user (audit `admin_rejected`).

NotFound.description: `not_found` — an unknown path resource (user, project, arm, event, instrument, field, or group).

Conflict.description: `conflict` — a state violation (§4.2): duplicate name, deletion that would strand data or leave zero enabled administrators, an expression-referenced delete, a mode transition outside the allowed set, staging conflicts, unacknowledged breaking changes.

RateLimited.description: 429 — the per-source-IP budget is exceeded; `Retry-After` names the remaining whole seconds of the blockout (REQ-API-038/113, §3.9).

Retry-After.description: Remaining whole seconds of the blockout, rounded up.

DataApiInvalidToken.description: Missing/invalid token — the same body whether or not the token exists (REQ-AUTH-032).

DataApiForbidden.description: `Permission denied` — insufficient permission (incl. export_none, read-only import); `Project in analysis mode` for writes to an analysis-mode project (GD-20, REQ-API-109).

Retry-After.description: Remaining whole seconds of the blockout, rounded up.

MetricsSnapshot.description: In-process performance snapshot (API_Endpoints_Design.md §4.25). Schema rule: fields may be added; existing field names and units never change.

generated_at.description: Canonical UTC timestamp of the snapshot.

process.description: Go runtime facts for this API process.

route.description: Server-side route template with method, e.g. `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`, `POST /api/`; `OTHER unmatched` when no pattern matched.

p50_ms.description: Histogram estimate: linear interpolation inside the bucket.

buckets_le_ms.description: Cumulative counts; the last entry is `+Inf` and equals `count`.

req_bytes_total.description: Sum of request body bytes (`ContentLength` when known, else counted).

calls.description: One entry per observed content value, sorted.

content.description: Fixed vocabulary value; `other` for anything a caller invented or omitted.

p50_ms.description: Histogram estimate: linear interpolation inside the bucket.

buckets_le_ms.description: Cumulative counts; the last entry is `+Inf` and equals `count`.

statements.description: One entry per verb seen, sorted.

p50_ms.description: Histogram estimate: linear interpolation inside the bucket.

buckets_le_ms.description: Cumulative counts; the last entry is `+Inf` and equals `count`.

rows_total.description: Rows the drivers reported: queries count rows read, writes `RowsAffected`; unknown counts contribute nothing.

wait_count.description: Cumulative pool waits — rises when the pool is the bottleneck.

le_ms.description: Upper bound in milliseconds, inclusive; the string `+Inf` on the last bucket.

enabled.description: Whether rate limiting is on (REQ-API-112) — lets a reader tell "nothing blocked" from "limiter off".

rpm.description: The effective per-minute budget per source IP.

block_minutes.description: The effective blockout period in minutes (REQ-API-113).

blocked.description: One entry per blocked source IP, sorted by address.

seconds_remaining.description: Whole seconds until the block expires, rounded up.

AdminError.description: The administration error shape (§4.2): `error` is a stable machine code callers may branch on; `message` is human-readable and never leaks internal details (REQ-API-006).

error.description: Stable machine code: invalid_request, validation_error, service_token_invalid, account_not_found, bad_password, invalid_setup_token, forbidden, account_disabled, account_expired, not_found, conflict, internal.

status.description: The HTTP status, mirrored in the body.

DataApiError.description: The data-API error body in JSON rendering (§3.2); with `returnFormat` csv (the default) the same text is a single CSV line.

DataApiRequest.description: The common data-API parameters (§3.1), `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Unknown parameters are accepted and ignored, never rejected (REQ-API-017). Indexed array syntax (`records[0]=…`) and repeated single values are both accepted (REQ-API-015). An indexed call carries one parameter per cell, so a batch is bounded at 250,000 parameters — about 1,250 rows of 200 fields; past that the call is refused 400 naming the limit, and the batch belongs in one `data` parameter holding a JSON array of record objects (REQ-API-144, REQ-API-031).

token.description: UUID project API token or survey-link token (§3.10). Body or query; never read from an Authorization header (REQ-API-010, REQ-AUTH-031).

action.description: With `content=record` only. `export`/`import` are accepted and never override the `data` rule; `delete` is the only action that dispatches; any other value → REDCap-style error (REQ-API-012, DEV-API-24).

format.description: `json` or `csv`; `csv` is REDCap's default rendering. A present `returnFormat` takes precedence (REQ-API-013).

returnFormat.description: A present returnFormat takes precedence for the response encoding (REQ-API-013).

type.description: `flat` is normative — one row per (record, event); `wide` is the simplified compatibility mode of §3.6.2 (DEV-API-1).

csvDelimiter.description: REDCap's set — tab as the character or by the name `tab`; empty value = comma. Any other value → 400 (REQ-API-029, REQ-EXP-013).

decimalCharacter.description: Record export: the decimal separator of calculated and floating-point values, in either format; empty value = the stored form (a period). Any other value → 400 (REQ-EXP-015).

records.description: Record identifiers to narrow the call to; sent as `records[0]=…` or repeated `records=…` (REQ-API-015). With `action=delete`, required — an unscoped delete is 400 (REQ-API-036).

fields.description: Field names to export or delete; sent as `fields[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). A checkbox named here covers all of its `<field>___<code>` columns (REQ-EXP-053, REQ-DB-042); a field-list export carries no `<instrument>_complete` column (REQ-API-134). The record identifier is always included even when left out (REQ-API-028).

forms.description: Instrument unique names; sent as `forms[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). A record export returns each named instrument's whole field block, ending with its `<instrument>_complete` column (REQ-API-134); `content=metadata`/`exportFieldNames` restrict the dictionary to these instruments (REQ-API-083, REQ-API-022).

events.description: Unique event names as returned by `content=event`; sent as `events[0]=…` or repeated (REQ-API-015). At an event an instrument is not mapped to the cell is empty (REQ-API-134).

filterLogic.description: Branching-logic expression (§3.6.3, Data_Validation_Design.md §7) filtering which records are returned; export only (REQ-API-025); never changes the sensitivity level.

rawOrLabel.description: Choice fields as codes or labels (REQ-API-027).

data.description: Import rows in either REDCap encoding (§3.7.1): the indexed form parameters `data[i][key]=…`, or a single `data` parameter holding a JSON array of record objects (DEV-API-24). Its presence makes the call an import (REQ-API-012, REQ-API-031). Indexed parameters win when both encodings are present. A row naming `redcap_repeat_instrument` and `redcap_repeat_instance` fills that instance of an instrument repeating at the row's event (REQ-API-155).

returnContent.description: With a record import: `count` answers `{"count": N}` for the rows applied; anything else keeps the §3.7.2 result rows (REQ-API-142).

repeat_instance.description: With `action=delete`: deletes one form instance only — `1` the first, `n` a further instance of a repeating instrument (REQ-API-155); without it every instance in scope goes. Not a positive integer → 400.

tz.description: IANA timezone name or ±HH:MM offset — timezone of collection for the call's date/date-time values; default APP_TIMEZONE (import only, GD-16, REQ-VAL-041).

overwriteBehavior.description: Accepted and ignored (REQ-API-017): import always upserts.

exportCheckboxLabel.description: Record export with `rawOrLabel=label`: `true` writes a checked box's choice label (unchecked: empty); otherwise REDCap's `Checked`/`Unchecked` (REQ-API-016, REQ-EXP-053).

ContentValue.description: The dispatcher of the data API (REQ-API-012). With `content=record`: a call carrying `data` is an import, one without it an export; deletion needs `action=delete`.

User.description: The user object (§4.3), returned by login and every user endpoint.

auth_source.description: The source the account last authenticated through (REQ-AUTH-005).

ui_theme.description: `null` when the account follows the installation default theme UI_THEME (GD-26).

last_login_at.description: `null` when the account has never logged in.

session_epoch.description: The account's session epoch (REQ-AUTH-074): the web layer stores it in the session at login and presents it as `X-Internal-Session-Epoch`; raised by every password write, every disable, an administrator's two-factor reset and a reported session replay. Counts revocations; authorizes nothing on its own.

provider.description: The identity provider (or LDAP source id) the PHP layer authenticated against.

password.description: Local login only; never logged (REQ-AUTH-036). Ignored on a race-finalizing call (REQ-API-135).

mfa_code.description: The second factor for the two-factor gate (GD-21).

first_factor.description: The handle from verify-password standing in for `password` on the second call of a two-factor challenge (REQ-API-131, DEV-API-19).

source_name.description: The authentication-source name the user selected; recorded in login audit details, never affects identity resolution or authorization (REQ-AUTH-067).

attempts.description: Per-source outcomes of a failed named-source credential race (source-id → outcome, e.g. bad_password, unreachable); MUST never contain credentials (REQ-AUTH-036). Such a call reports a failure and authenticates nothing (REQ-API-135).

first_factor.description: Only on `ok` for an account a second factor still guards: stateless handle bound to one user id, signed with a key derived from INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN (REQ-API-131).

password.description: Optional — stored only as an argon2id hash (REQ-AUTH-050), never returned or logged.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Any subset; idempotent (REQ-API-042). Any change leaving zero enabled administrators → 409 (REQ-AUTH-068, REQ-API-136).

password.description: Set/reset the local hash; an empty string clears it (REQ-AUTH-036).

secret.description: Base32 shared secret — shown once, pending until confirmed (REQ-AUTH-056).

code.description: A current RFC 6238 code, an emailed confirmation code, or a recovery code (disable).

role.description: `null` for a role-less member (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022).

MemberWithToken.description: The token value appears only in the add/rotation response — never in logs (REQ-API-005) and never in audit details.

MemberMutation.description: The single mutation point for membership (REQ-API-054): add (`role`), change role (`role`, `null` = role-less), rotate the token (`rotate_token`), remove (`remove`).

role.description: Role name; null or omitted = role-less (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022).

arms.description: Per-arm default; keys are arm numbers as strings; every arm of the project appears (REQ-AUTH-019).

grants.description: Only the (instrument, event) pairs whose grant differs from their arm default (REQ-AUTH-069).

delete_values.description: The delete-instrument-values right — a boolean, never a level (REQ-AUTH-070).

RoleInput.description: The role object minus `id` (POST and PUT — REQ-API-143). An arm absent from `arms` defaults to no_access / export_none.

ProjectCreate.description: The creation fields of the simplified `projects` (GD-17, REQ-DB-006). The removed attributes (`end_provision`, `option_*`, `agreed_to_end_user_contract`, `event_names`) are rejected as unknown attributes (400, REQ-API-052).

ProjectUpdate.description: Any subset of the creation metadata fields — omitted fields are unchanged (idempotent, REQ-API-042).

ProjectDetail.description: Full metadata plus structure plus the acting user's effective permissions (REQ-API-126).

EffectivePermissions.description: The effective evaluation of Authentication_Authorization_Design.md §4.1 for the acting user — one `arms[]` entry per arm carrying that arm's default, one `grants[]` entry per mapped (instrument, event) pair as it resolves for that caller; nothing is ever absent from either list (REQ-AUTH-069).

period.description: Timepoint — days after baseline; `null` = no timepoint (GD-15).

EventUpdate.description: Any subset; `period: null` clears the timepoint (GD-15). A label change re-derives unique_event_name — a collision → 409.

repeating_events.description: The events the instrument repeats at (REQ-API-154) — arms by number, events in canonical order; `[]` when none.

field_name.description: Lower-case alphanumeric + underscore, unique within the project.

field_type.description: text, notes, dropdown, radio, checkbox, yesno, matrix, description, header or calculated (REQ-DB-013). A yesno field always stores the choices 1$Yes##0$No (REQ-DB-043); yesno and notes keep no validation type (REQ-DB-044).

choices.description: Stored `code$label##code$label` encoding for choice fields; codes are letters, digits, - and _ (a checkbox: lower-case letters, digits and _). Writes also accept REDCap's `code, label | code, label` form (REQ-VAL-022).

validation_type.description: Empty, a built-in structured type, or a validation_types registry name (REQ-VAL-010/042).

field_annotation.description: REDCap action tags and notes, stored as given; @READONLY makes the field read-only in forms and surveys (REQ-DB-046).

direct_identifier.description: Defaults to true for email, MRN, international phone, national phone (REQ-EXP-020).

FieldInput.description: The field object minus `id`/`position` (appended at the end of the list).

field_annotation.description: REDCap action tags and notes, stored as given; @READONLY makes the field read-only in forms and surveys (REQ-DB-046).

FieldUpdate.description: Any subset of the attributes — including a field_name rename (stored values renamed in the same transaction, REQ-VAL-014), the calculation expression (triggers recomputation, REQ-VAL-037), the branching logic and the direct_identifier flag.

field_annotation.description: REDCap action tags and notes, stored as given; @READONLY makes the field read-only in forms and surveys (REQ-DB-046).

acknowledge_breaking.description: Analysis mode only (REQ-API-111): re-send after a 409 naming the breaking change.

InstrumentImportResult.description: The §4.10 import result. Warning codes: renamed, skipped, dropped_attribute, converted, long_name, ignored_entry. Problem codes: form_not_contiguous, identifier_not_value, unsupported_type, invalid_csv, invalid_archive, missing_column, missing_instrument_csv, validation_error.

existing.description: The project's empty first instrument, which receives the first field.

acknowledge_breaking.description: Read from the top level of the body (analysis mode, REQ-API-111).

regex.description: Advisory client-side hint only — server-side validation remains authoritative (REQ-VAL-002).

mapping.description: instrument name → the unique_event_names it is mapped to; an empty array = mapped to no event.

instruments.description: Only the cells that are not `no_data` (REQ-API-149); a mapped instrument absent here is `no_data`.

state.description: The first instance's state; `no_data` only on a repeating instrument whose further instances hold something.

instances.description: A repeating instrument only (REQ-API-156): every instance whose state is not `no_data`, ascending.

target_record.description: The record of a record-scoped event (record_created, record_updated, record_deleted, calculated_recomputed, survey_submitted, dag_record_assigned, …); null for every other event.

details.description: Entries MAY carry the token column and payload values — the trail is the sole sanctioned carrier (REQ-AUD-007).

instance.description: The form instance — 1 for every form that does not repeat (REQ-API-156).

new.description: `null` for delete — the `old` values are the deleted values (REQ-AUD-009).

state.description: `none` — nothing issued for the pair; `submitted` — its one submission arrived, which is also what spent the link (REQ-API-145).

url.description: The public link carrying the link token — a value only while the link is live, since handing out a spent token's URL would only send a respondent to a 410. One link per (project, record, instrument, event).

collected_at.description: `null` until a response is saved through the link, then never changes (REQ-DB-041, REQ-AUTH-071).

strings.description: Flat key→text map; a missing key renders in English (REQ-DB-031).

breaking.description: Classification per the normative table of §4.21.

rate_limit_rpm.description: Requests per rolling minute per source IP (default 600).

rate_limit_block_minutes.description: Blockout after exceeding the budget (default 10; REQ-API-113).

api_listen_loopback.description: API_ADDR binds a loopback address only.

running_as_root.description: The API process runs with effective user id 0; null where the platform has none.

password_unchanged.description: The ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL account still signs in with that password; null when it is not set or no such account exists.

clock_synchronized.description: The kernel clock is synchronized to a time source (adjtimex); null off Linux.

selinux.description: null off Linux or when unreadable.

version.description: VERSION() on MariaDB, sqlite_version() on SQLite.

grants.description: The application account's effective privileges on its schema (global, schema and table grants; roles are not followed).

audit_writable.description: Audit tables the account may UPDATE, DELETE or DROP — empty in the runtime state of REQ-DB-024.

tables_missing_write.description: Other base tables without UPDATE and DELETE.

drop.description: DROP held at schema or global level.

audit_partitions.description: Partition names per audit table (`p2026`, …); an unpartitioned table maps to an empty list.
